selected_problem: After preexisting-index ownership and pre-commit index-postimage checks were closed, fresh main still trusted the final `git commit` operation itself. Git hooks or a concurrent index mutation can change staged bytes or add unrelated paths after the index integrity check but before the immutable commit object is created, allowing a local delivery commit to diverge from the validation receipt.

decision_provenance.mode_route_basis: The new main left one narrow, deterministic and central delivery artifact gap: the checked Git index was not yet bound to the immutable commit object. The committed four-mode router therefore routes this singular evidence-rich bottleneck to DEEP_DEVELOPMENT without forced rotation.
decision_provenance.claim_limit: No hosted DWAC/UPDIA success receipt or fabricated numeric score is claimed.

sequence: Create and validate run-owned a.txt as `validated`.
Stage a.txt so the existing index-postimage check would pass.
Install an executable pre-commit hook that rewrites a.txt to `hook-mutated` and stages it.
Run ordinary git commit as current gitLocalCommit does.
Observed immutable HEAD:a.txt is `hook-mutated`, proving final commit bytes can diverge after the pre-commit integrity point.

changes: gitLocalCommit now captures the parent HEAD before staging and, after a successful commit, verifies the immutable commit tree against the validation receipt.
The final commit check compares existence, SHA-256 content, Git-representable executable mode, and the complete changed-path ownership set between parent and new commit.
If hooks or concurrent staging alter run-owned bytes or introduce unrelated paths, delivery fails closed with GIT_COMMIT_POSTIMAGE_DRIFT.

Because the preexisting Git index was already required to be clean, a failed final-artifact check safely resets the local branch to its captured parent with `git reset --mixed`, preserving working-tree bytes while removing the rejected local commit and staged state.
Clean validated commits continue normally and now carry commitIntegrity evidence.

validation.tests: 7/7 focused Git delivery regressions PASS on the Linux verification host
new_reality_cases: pre-commit hook mutates and stages run-owned bytes: rejected, HEAD restored to parent, index cleared, mutated working bytes preserved
pre-commit hook stages an unrelated path: rejected by commit ownership check, HEAD restored to parent, index cleared, working bytes preserved
validation.verification_scope_note: The local harness exercises the exact modified Git index/commit integrity functions and all seven repository Git-delivery regression cases. Unchanged GitHub remote API helpers were intentionally not executed and no Actions were used.

truth_boundaries: This binds the immutable local commit tree to the validation receipt and run-owned path set. Working-tree files may still be changed by hooks after the commit; those changes are not part of the accepted commit artifact and remain visible for later repair/revalidation.
The rollback uses a local mixed reset only after the earlier clean-index gate, so it does not claim to preserve arbitrary independently staged state appearing concurrently after that gate.
Git commit-tree verification covers Git-recorded file content and executable mode, not full filesystem metadata such as ownership, ACLs, xattrs, timestamps or hard-link topology.
OS-level validation sandboxing, arbitrary complex semantic synthesis, Windows descendant-tree equivalence, and crash-level filesystem atomicity remain unresolved.
No GitHub Actions are intentionally triggered or rerun, no force push is used, and no credential, payment, formal Release, or destructive/irreversible external action is performed.
